newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end up on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end up on selective buying.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended up on Tuesday on selective buying, but trading volume has yet to pick up significantly with most investors awaiting the issue of more 1996 company results, brokers said.
The Shanghai B share index ended up at a year-high with domestic investors buying Pudong real estate-related stocks after A shares reversed early losses, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.756 points or 1.02 percent to 74.895 points on volume of 13.95 million shares worth $7.9 million, compared with $8.8 million on Monday.
Shanghai Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development gained $0.016 or 3.34 percent to $0.494 on volume of 678,300 shares.

Another Pudong stock, Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development, the most actively traded counter, also erased early losses, to end up $0.002 or 0.19 percent at $1.032 on volume of 1.3 million shares. "Pudong is waiting to celebrate its seventh anniversary (since its establishment in 1990 as Shanghai's premier economic development zone) and that was used by some domestic investors as an excuse to boost the market," one broker said.
"But follow-up buying was limited due to concerns over results that have yet to be released," he said.
Shanghai Tyre & Rubber was the star performer on expectations of improved results in 1996, up $0.026 or 5.43 percent to $0.504 on volume of 687,100 shares.

Shenzhen's B share index ended up 0.25 points or 0.15 percent at 159.52 points on selective buying of companies that have already issued favourable 1996 annual results. Turnover was HK$90.4 million against Monday's HK$83.8 million.
Shenzhen Lionda Holdings Co Ltd was the top performer, gaining HK$0.23 or 6.39 percent to HK$3.83 on volume of 10,940 shares.
The Shanghai A share index ended up after a technical correction in the morning, as market sentiment remained positive, brokers said.
The index gained 8.298 points or 0.60 percent to 1,389.752 points on volume of 938.2 million shares and turnover of 11.4 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index added 14.810 points or 0.41 percent to 3,596.396 points.
Yunnan Malong Chemicals & Construction was the star on institutional buying, soaring 1.35 yuan or 10.02 percent to 14.81 yuan on volume of 2.4 million shares.
The Shenzhen A share index ended 0.74 points or 0.16 percent higher to 459.83 on turnover of 7.74 billion yuan against 8.4 billion yuan on Monday.
